text:
alex: Nightly GPU CI flagged a bunch of failures on the multi-arch runners, looks like OOMs + a weird kernel warn. Filing here to coordinate bisect. @maya can you take a look?

maya: on it. which test suite? ephemeral or integration? :eyes:

alex: integration/gpu/**/* — failing tests cluster around `alloc_kv_cache` and `runtime_infer_smoke`. Most failures show `CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN` in logs, then dmesg prints an Xid 31 on some nodes.

ivan: CI rerun just finished (manually) and some nodes passed, others consistently fail. suspects: driver/runtime mismatch or a new kernel module churn. Can we get `nvidia-smi` + container runtime versions from failing hosts?

ci-bot: re-run queued by @alex — build 2026.03.17-nightly #4572. Logs available: https://ci.internal/redwood/4572 (archived)

maya: grabbed outputs from two failing nodes, paste below.

maya: ```
# node gpu-ml-12: failing
$ nvidia-smi
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12 Driver Version: 525.85.12 CUDA Version: 12.1       |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

# container runtime (inside job)
$ cat /proc/1/comm
containerd
$ strings /proc/self/environ | grep -i cuda
CUDA_VERSION=11.8

# dmesg tail
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, Ch 00000001, intr 10000000.
[ 1234.568012] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU is busy but client has been terminated
```

maya: so host drivers report 525/CUDA12.1 but the job environment has CUDA 11.8 libs — possible runtime/driver mismatch causing unknown errors.

jordan: that mismatch would explain intermittent behavior when we use prebuilt containers with older CUDA. We recently promoted a container image to nightly that includes CUDA 11.8 libs for inference runtime.

alex: good find. Two asks: 1) can we mark the nightly job to pin a compat driver (or switch to a 11.8-compatible host image) so it stays green while we triage? 2) can someone bisect the image promotion so we know which image introduced the mismatch?

ivan: I'll pin the job to the legacy-11-compat host pool for a quick mitigation. Doing that now.

ivan: done — job rerun pinned to legacy-11-compat pool. queued. :hammer:

maya: for bisect, we should get the manifest of the promoted image and the digest history. I can query the registry and run a local container replicate to repro quickly.

alex: please also capture a failing core dump (if any) and a `gdb --batch -ex 'bt full'` on the inference worker if it crashes. We need to know if it's OOM from allocation mismatch or driver abort.

maya: noted. I also recommend enabling `--nv-host-logs` for the job so we can gather `dmesg`/`nvidia-smi --query` snapshots automatically next time.

ci-bot: rerun started (legacy-11-compat) by @ivan — build 4572.retry. Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/4572/retry

alex: if retry passes, we'll treat this as a compatibility fallout from the promoted runtime image and revert promotion. If it still fails, we need a deeper bisect across kernel/driver changes.

jordan: FYI I opened a registry ticket with image digests and promotion timeline: REG-1291. Adding manifests now.

maya: quick repro locally: when I launch the image on current hosts with CUDA11 libs + driver 525, the container sees `CUDA_VERSION=11.8` but the runtime loader links to libcuda.so from host which is 525 (CUDA12 headers). This can cause subtle allocation ABI differences and fail on bigger allocation patterns (KV cache warmup).

ivan: retry finished: all tests in this job are green on legacy pool. Looks like mitigation worked.

alex: great. next steps: 1) revert promotion of the 11.8-nightly image until we've validated compatibility across our host driver matrix, 2) add an automated preflight that checks container CUDA runtime vs host driver compatibility before promotion (simple `nvidia-smi --query` + container `CUDA_VERSION` compare), 3) run bisect on registry images to find minimal diff and add test coverage.

jordan: I can own the promotion revert + registry bisect. Will post commits/PRs.

maya: I'll open a short runbook snippet on the incident and add the `--nv-host-logs` flag as part of job templates on eng-ml.

alex: thanks everyone. adding a follow-up card in our board and linking REG-1291 and CI job 4572. :white_check_mark:

ivan: thumbs up. let's close after promotion is reverted and preflight is in place.

jordan: opening PR now, pinging infra for expedited review.

maya: leaving logs and gdb output in the ticket.

alex: closing thread — keep updates in REG-1291 or board card.
